result.title: Calibrated Decision Rewards: Training Language Models with a Judge That Knows How Sure It Is
result.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) can only teach a language model what its reward can recognize. Answer checkers are exact but need a reference answer; learned reward models and LLM judges work everywhere, but their scores are not probabilities. We study RLCDR (Reinforcement Learning from Calibrated Decision Rewards). An LLM converted into a decision model answers a typed question about a response ("is the final answer correct?", "which step is the first error?") with a probability distribution, read in one forward pass, debiased over option orders and calibrated with about a hundred labels. Training Qwen3-1.7B with GRPO on MATH, this reference-free reward raises MATH500 accuracy from 72.2% to 76.8% (+4.65 points, p < 1e-4), matching training on the answer key (76.9%), while a random reward gains only +0.65. The gain grows with difficulty, from 44.8% to 51.7% on the hardest level. On the policy's own changing samples the reward stays calibrated: its expected calibration error is half that of a softmax judge on the same 27B backbone (0.074 vs. 0.141), and it shows no sign of reward hacking. Without step training, the same model finds the first wrong step better than a dedicated 7B process reward model (ProcessBench F1 0.772 vs. 0.722, 20/20 splits). We also map where the approach stops being enough: trained only on problems the base model mostly fails, the reference-free reward still improves the policy (+1.9 MATH500 points, p = 0.03) but trails the answer key, because its probabilities become overconfident on that distribution. We state six hypotheses in advance and test each with a control designed to falsify it.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 RLCDR：把 LLM 改造成对「答案是否正确」「首个错误步骤是哪一步」这类问题给出概率分布的决策模型，经选项顺序去偏与约百条标注校准后，作为无参考答案的 RL 奖励，在 Qwen3-1.7B 上用 GRPO 训练数学推理，并标出该奖励在分布偏移下过度自信的失效边界。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本的奖励校准工作，但「单次前向读出首错步骤概率并作为密集训练信号」可能为 latent 推理轨迹的步骤级贡献分配与训练监督提供线索，其校准与 reward hacking 诊断也值得核查能否迁移到多模态判据。
